text: . Indian astronomers, along with their international collaborators, have reported the rare discovery of a Blue Straggler Star (BSS) caught in the act of formation. This has provided direct evidence of how such stars are created.Blue Straggler Stars (BSS) are a peculiar class of stars found in star clusters that appear hotter, brighter, and more massive than their peers. The Ministry of Science and Technology informed that astronomers have sought to understand their origin and evolution for a long time.The Ministry said that the most widely accepted explanation is that these stars gain mass from a companion or through stellar mergers, effectively rejuvenating themselves. Direct observational evidence of such formation processes has remained extremely rare.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said that innovation, deep technologies, startups, MSMEs and globally competitive manufacturing will drive India’s next phase of economic growth and help realise the vision of a developed India by 2047.Addressing the 22nd J.R.D. Tata Memorial Lecture in New Delhi, Mr Goyal said the country must strive for excellence and ensure that Made in India products earn global respect through quality, innovation and competitiveness.The Minister highlighted several initiatives to promote innovation, including the one lakh crore rupee Research, Development and Innovation Fund, the IndiaAI Mission and the Second Semiconductor Mission. He said these initiatives will further strengthen the country’s innovation ecosystem and accelerate the development of emerging technologies.Mr Goyal said the Government is creating an enabling business environment by reducing the compliance burden, decriminalising outdated laws and improving the ease of doing business. He added that skill development should become an industry-led movement, supported by the Government through an enabling ecosystem. The Minister noted that India continues to remain the world’s fastest-growing major economy despite global uncertainties.Calling upon industry to invest more in research, innovation and skill development, Mr Goyal urged entrepreneurs and investors to support home-grown deep-tech startups at an early stage and help them move from innovation to commercialisation and global scale.The Commerce and Industry Minister also paid tribute to J.R.D. Tata, saying his vision of excellence, innovation and nation-building continues to inspire Indian industry. He expressed confidence that these values will help realise the vision of a developed India by 2047.

. Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu reviewed the country’s preparedness for the adoption of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and implementation of the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA). Chairing a high-level meeting in New Delhi, the Minister reviewed the country’s roadmap for SAF production, blending, carbon accounting and supply chain development ahead of the mandatory phase of CORSIA from 1st January next year.The Ministry of Civil Aviation said the meeting reviewed the progress of Sustainable Aviation Fuel production projects being implemented by Oil Marketing Companies, certification processes and measures to ensure timely availability of SAF to meet the anticipated demand from 2027. The meeting also discussed the proposed SAF blending roadmap, development of a national SAF Registry with end-to-end traceability, and a robust accounting, monitoring and reporting framework aligned with ICAO requirements.Speaking on the occasion, Mr Naidu said the government is committed to building a globally competitive Sustainable Aviation Fuel ecosystem that supports the growth of the aviation sector while contributing to global decarbonisation efforts. The Minister said the draft Sustainable Aviation Fuel Policy is in its final stages and is being finalised through consultations with stakeholders.

. The annual Kanwar Yatra for the Shravan month will begin today. During the Kanwar Yatra, a large number of people visit pilgrimage sites such as Haridwar, Gaumukh and Gangotri in Uttarakhand to fetch holy water from the Ganga River. The Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh governments have made elaborate arrangements to manage the large number of pilgrims.In Uttar Pradesh, traffic diversions have been implemented in several districts to ensure the smooth movement of Kanwariyas and other commuters. In Lucknow, DCP Traffic Ravina Tyagi said that traffic diversions have been put in place on several routes in the state capital for one month in view of the Kanwar Yatra.Keeping the convenience of passengers in mind during the Kanwar Yatra, NCRTC has decided to increase the frequency of Namo Bharat train services in the National Capital Region. For devotees travelling to Deoghar, the Railways has announced two special Shravan Mela trains from Gorakhpur.In Ayodhya, administrative officials inspected Ram Ki Paidi and the Naya Ghat area to review arrangements for devotees.In Varanasi, Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham Temple Trust CEO Vishwabhushan Mishra said that special arrangements have been made for the convenience and safety of pilgrims. These include shaded zig-zag queues, distribution of glucose water and ORS. Flower showers will also be organised for devotees in the morning.

. The Reserve Bank of India has said that the operations of Paytm Payments Bank Limited will be wound up and has appointed former Chief General Manager of SBI, Girikumar Nair, as the Official Liquidator. The central bank said the decision follows the orders of the Delhi High Court allowing the winding-up of the bank as per the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, and the Companies Act, 2013.The RBI had announced the cancellation of the banking licence of Paytm Payments Bank, citing serious regulatory violations and concerns over the manner in which the bank’s affairs were conducted. The banking regulator had earlier clarified that despite the winding-up process, Paytm Payments Bank had sufficient liquidity to repay its entire deposit liabilities.

. The Union Health Ministry today observed World Hepatitis Day 2026, marking 8 years of the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP). The programme, launched in 2018 under the National Health Mission, aims to eliminate viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals.Addressing the event in New Delhi, Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare Anupriya Patel reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to achieving a Hepatitis-Mukt Bharat. She said India is among the few countries providing free treatment for Hepatitis C and free management of Hepatitis B. She added that hepatitis screening and treatment services have now been expanded to more than one lakh 85 thousand Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, improving access to care across the country.The Minister said Hepatitis B birth-dose vaccination coverage has crossed 92 per cent. She urged States and Union Territories to ensure 100 per cent screening of pregnant women for Hepatitis B and to step up awareness on Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C for early detection and timely treatment. On the occasion, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava said that under the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme, over 21 crore people have been screened, more than six lakh patients treated and one thousand 153 treatment centres established across the country. She added that over seven crore 64 lakh pregnant women have also been screened under the programme.During the event, the Ministry also released Information, Education and Communication materials on viral hepatitis, highlighting its modes of transmission and the services available under the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme for wider dissemination across States and Union Territories.

. Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia today reviewed the progress of the Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) in New Delhi and reiterated the government’s commitment to making India a global leader in 6G technologies. The review focused on the progress made by the Bharat 6G Alliance towards achieving Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of making India a front-line contributor in the design, development and deployment of 6G technology by 2030. The Alliance is working through seven specialised groups covering areas such as spectrum, technology, applications, sustainability, manufacturing, outreach and 6G use cases.On the occasion, Mr Scindia stressed the need to benchmark India’s 6G progress against global developments and strengthen collaboration among the Alliance’s working groups. He emphasised that India’s 6G journey must be driven by indigenous research, global standards participation, domestic manufacturing and strong partnerships among government, industry, academia, startups and research institutions.

. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan congratulated Sharmila Dhankar on winning gold in the Women’s Shot Put F57 event, becoming India’s first-ever Commonwealth Games Gold medallist in Para Athletics. The Vice President also congratulated Sarvesh Anil Kushare on securing silver in Men’s High Jump. He also extended best wishes to Valluri Ajaya Babu on claiming silver in Men’s 79kg weightlifting.Further, Mr Radhakrishnan congratulated Shilpa K. Shyla on earning bronze in the Women’s Shot Put F57 event at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games. Sharing a social media post, the Vice President said that their remarkable achievements have brought immense pride to the nation and will inspire generations of athletes. He wished them all continued success and many more laurels in the years ahead.

. The Lok Sabha has passed the anti-Paper leak bill, proposing tougher penalties and fast-track courts to curb examination malpractices. The Bill seeks to amend the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 incorporates several significant provisions, including stringent penalties such as imprisonment for up to ten years, fines of up to ten crore rupees, and seizure of the properties of convicted offenders. The legislation mandates every State Government and Union Territory Administration to establish Special Fast Track Courts for day-to-day trials.Replying to the discussion on the Bill, Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Dr Jitendra Singh said the amendment has been brought to make the law more stringent and ensure speedy justice in paper leak cases.After the passage of the Bill, the Lower House was adjourned till 11 AM today.

. Global crude oil prices jumped more than four per cent today amid renewed tensions in West Asia. Brent crude was trading over 4.8 per cent up at 88 US dollars and 16 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 4.4 per cent up at 82 US dollars and 76 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. India’s total exports reached a record 863.1 billion US dollars in the financial year 2025-26. The government informed Parliament yesterday that the surge was driven by strong growth in both merchandise and services exports and supported by expanding market access under the country’s free trade agreements (FTAs).According to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, merchandise exports stood at 441.8 billion dollars, while services exports reached 421.3 billion dollars, reflecting the combined strength of both sectors in driving the country’s export growth. The Ministry said India’s recent trade agreements have significantly expanded export opportunities, particularly with the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the United Kingdom, Australia, Oman and EFTA countries, while also helping diversify export markets and strengthen labour-intensive sectors.Among FTA partners, merchandise exports in the financial year 2025-26 were highest to ASEAN countries at 38.42 billion dollars, followed by the UAE at 37.36 billion dollars, SAFTA countries, the UK and Singapore. The Ministry highlighted the growing utilisation of India’s recently operationalised trade agreements through the increasing use of Certificates of Origin and wider product coverage.

. President Donald Trump held separate meetings with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House yesterday. Both meetings took place behind closed doors in the Oval Office.White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, in a social media post, said President Trump had concluded his meetings with President Zelensky and Prime Minister Netanyahu and that both meetings were positive and productive. This was the first meeting between Mr Netanyahu and Mr Trump since they launched a joint war against Iran. Their meeting lasted nearly an hour, and the White House and the Prime Minister’s Office did not immediately offer more details.In a post on social media, Mr Zelensky thanked Mr Trump for the good meeting and the Republican administration’s efforts to aid Kyiv in the long-running war, which began more than four years ago when Russia invaded Ukraine. Mr Zelensky arrived in Washington seeking progress on sanctions against Russia, a drone agreement, Patriot air defence systems and peace talks. He was also expected to meet lawmakers and address a gathering of the full Senate.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Sharmila for winning a gold medal in the Women’s Shot Put F57 event and also for a season-best throw at the Commonwealth Games (CWG) in Glasgow. In a social media post, he called the performance remarkable, which ended a two-decade-long wait for a Para Athletics Gold at the Commonwealth Games. He also congratulated Valluri Ajaya Babu for winning the Silver Medal in the weightlifting Men’s 79 kg category at the Commonwealth Games (CWG) in Glasgow.The Prime Minister said that the weightlifter etched his name in the record books by setting a CWG Record in the Snatch event. Mr Modi further congratulated Sarvesh Anil Kushare for clinching the Silver Medal in the Men’s High Jump event at the Commonwealth Games 2026. The Prime Minister extended his best wishes to all the medalists for many more inspiring feats.

. Union Minister for Communications Jyotiraditya Scindia has launched the theme for the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 in New Delhi. The 10th edition of Asia’s largest digital technology forum will be held from 7th to 10th October in New Delhi.Organised by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and the Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI), IMC 2026 will bring together global technology leaders, telecom operators, innovators, startups, investors, researchers and policymakers to shape the next phase of India’s digital transformation.Speaking on the occasion, Mr Scindia said the theme, ‘Scale without Boundaries’, reflects India’s ambition to take its telecom innovations, technologies and digital solutions beyond national borders for global benefit. He said the next phase of India’s telecom journey should focus on exporting home-grown innovations and shaping global technology standards.Mr Scindia said nearly 500 million people have been connected to 5G services within two-and-a-half years through investments of about 4.5 lakh crore rupees and the rollout of around five lakh telecom towers. He expressed confidence that 6G technology will integrate physical, digital and intelligence ecosystems, with India aiming to become a global leader in the field.The Minister also said the 10th edition of IMC is anchored around four key pillars — Srishti (Building the Future), Suraksha (Strengthening Trust), Sashakt (Expanding Opportunities) and Samvardhan (Fueling Growth) — reflecting India’s vision of building a digitally empowered, secure and growth-oriented future.Mr Scindia also highlighted initiatives such as the Bharat 6G Alliance, the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for telecom manufacturing and the Sanchar Saathi portal, saying these are strengthening innovation, domestic manufacturing and digital security. He said IMC 2026 will showcase emerging technologies, including 5G, 6G, Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, satellite communications, cloud and edge computing, quantum technologies and green technologies.Addressing the gathering, Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, said the past decade has been unprecedented for India’s telecom sector and the India Mobile Congress provides a global platform to showcase the country’s achievements in telecommunications. He added that IMC also serves as a platform for collaboration between the government and industry, enabling startups to showcase their innovations while providing investors with opportunities to support India’s growing digital ecosystem.

. Major Asian stock markets closed mixed today. South Korea’s Kospi index plunged six per cent as investors continued selling semiconductor shares. Earlier in the session, the Korea Exchange halted trading for 20 minutes after activating a circuit breaker for the second consecutive day. This marks the eighth circuit breaker activation by the exchange so far this year.Taiwan’s Taiex shed almost 3.8 per cent, and Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell one and a half per cent. In contrast, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index climbed nearly two per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times index gained over 1.7 per cent, and China’s Shanghai Composite rose 0.4 per cent.Major European indices were displayed mixed trend today. Germany’s DAX as well as London’s FTSE 100 increased by 0.3 per cent, while France’s CAC 40 dipped nearly half a per cent, when reports last came in.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal held a meeting with Export Promotion Councils and Industry Associations in New Delhi to review measures aimed at strengthening India’s export ecosystem.In a social media post, Mr Goyal said the meeting followed discussions on enhancing the country’s global competitiveness. During the meeting, the Minister reaffirmed the government’s commitment to building a stronger, more competitive and future-ready export ecosystem to support India’s economic growth and realise the vision of Viksit Bharat.The meeting focused on leveraging Free Trade Agreements, promoting the Brand India initiative through quality-led exports, improving logistics and trade facilitation, expanding market access, and creating new opportunities for MSMEs and new exporters.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said that India’s merchandise exports have registered 15 per cent growth so far in the current financial year, despite the Red Sea crisis and global turmoil.He said that despite these headwinds, India’s merchandise exports have grown by 15 per cent during the April-July period. Delivering the JRD Tata Memorial Lecture 2026, Mr Goyal said the country’s merchandise exports remained resilient despite mounting geopolitical tensions and disruptions to global trade routes.The Minister said India’s export performance reflects the strength of the country’s economic fundamentals, even as businesses worldwide grapple with uncertainty stemming from conflicts in West Asia and disruptions in key shipping corridors.The Minister said the first quarter of the current financial year has been marked by persistent global challenges, including volatility in crude oil, petrol, diesel and gas markets, as well as uncertainty surrounding the Strait of Hormuz and the continuing Red Sea crisis.Highlighting India’s broader economic performance, Mr Goyal said the country remained the world’s fastest-growing major economy, recording 7.7 per cent growth in the previous financial year despite a lot of uncertainty around the world.

. India scripted history in para athletics at the Commonwealth Games, securing a historic one-two finish in the men’s 100-metre T47 final, with Dilip Mahadu Gavit winning gold and Mohammed Basil Morssinganakath claiming silver.Gavit clocked a Games record and season-best time of 10.71 seconds to take the top spot, while Basil produced his season-best time of 10.83 seconds to finish second in a closely fought race. England’s Kevin Santos completed the podium with 10.85 seconds to win the bronze medal.These medals were India’s third and fourth medals of the day, after long jumper Murali Sreeshankar had earlier opened the day’s account with a silver in the men’s long jump. The silver medal also made Sreeshankar the first Indian men’s long jumper to win two Commonwealth Games medals.The gold was India’s third at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, following Mirabai Chanu’s victory in the women’s 48-kilogram weightlifting event and Sharmila Dhankar’s triumph in the women’s shot put F57 para athletics category. The medals lifted India to eighth spot in the standings, taking its overall tally to 15 medals — three gold, nine silver and three bronze.President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Dilip Mahadu Gavit on winning the Gold Medal and Mohammed Basil Morssinganakathi on securing the Silver Medal in the Men’s 100-metre T47 event at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games 2026.

. Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) has charged Telegram founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorist activities and has started the process of placing him on the international wanted list, according to Russian state media.The FSB alleges that Telegram failed to remove channels, chats and bots that were allegedly used by Ukrainian intelligence to plan attacks inside Russia. Authorities also claim that Telegram’s dating service was used to recruit Russians for terrorist activities. It is also said that an international warrant for his arrest has been issued.According to Russian legal experts, Durov could face arrest in absentia as part of the legal process to seek his extradition through Interpol. Russian media also reported that the charges could carry a life sentence if he is convicted. Durov has not publicly responded to these latest charges.Durov has previously faced legal action in France over allegations related to illegal content on Telegram, including child sexual abuse material, fraud and drug trafficking.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended over one per cent higher today. The Sensex surged 889 points to close at 77,655. The Nifty gained 265 points to settle at 24,250.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index rose over 0.8 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index jumped nearly one and a half per cent.Earlier, the markets opened higher, with stronger-than-expected industrial production growth data providing the catalyst for a positive start. Both benchmark indices sustained their upward momentum throughout the session, supported by renewed risk appetite.In the Sensex pack, 25 out of 30 companies registered gains. Among the top performers, Hindustan Unilever climbed 4.7 per cent, Infosys rose four and a half per cent and Trent added over two and a half per cent. In contrast, Adani Ports shed 3.2 per cent, Mahindra and Mahindra dipped one and a half per cent and PowerGrid lost 0.9 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 20 out of 27 sectors ended in positive zone. Among the top gainers, IT rose 2.4 per cent, Metal advanced almost 2.3 per cent, and Focused IT gained 1.9 per cent. In contrast, MidSmall Private Banks Quality Tilt fell over 0.6 per cent, Services dropped half a per cent, and Realty dipped 0.3 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2 thousand 593 companies advanced, 1 thousand 652 declined, and 179 remained unchanged.

. The Embassy of India in Kyiv, Ukraine, has said that the situation regarding MV AMIR1, with Indian seafarers onboard, is its highest priority. The Embassy said it is in constant touch with all concerned to ensure the safety and security of all Indians onboard. The Embassy shared this information through a social media post.

. In the Indian bullion market, 24 carat Gold was trading 0.1 per cent down at 1,42,060 rupees per 10 grams, while Silver was trading over 0.1 per cent down at 2,16,140 rupees per kilogram, a short while ago.On the Multi Commodity Exchange, Gold for the August contract was trading 0.2 per cent down at 1,41,323 rupees per 10 grams, and Silver for the September contract was trading nearly 0.2 per cent down at 2,15,485 rupees per kilogram, when reports last came in.

. The National Testing Agency (NTA) has issued advertisements for a set of senior professional appointments at the level of General Manager. It has also opened the engagement of sixteen young professionals through the Pratibha Setu portal of the Union Public Service Commission. NTA in a statement said that these measures represent the first concrete step in the institutional rebuild of the agency that is being implemented in line with the recommendations of the High-Level Committee of Experts chaired by Prof. K. Radhakrishnan.NTA has notified four Positions for General Manager on contract, each for an initial term of three years. The General Manager, Assessment Research and Development and Psychometrics, will head NTA’s academic and measurement-science function. The General Manager, Test Centre Network and Operations, will lead NTA’s nationwide test-centre footprint, spanning over five hundred cities and select international centres, with responsibility for empanelment standards, capacity planning, and centre quality. The General Manager, Information Security, designated as NTA’s Chief Information Security Officer, will head the cyber-security function of the Agency. The General Manager, Vigilance, Investigation and Forensics, will head NTA’s internal vigilance, investigations and digital forensics function.The NTA said that the engagement of Young Professionals is being undertaken for the first time. The Agency added that further recruitment and empanelment actions across the ten functional verticals recommended by the High-Level Committee of Experts will follow in the coming weeks.

. The government has said that the country became free from Left Wing Extremism after nearly six decades of violence, which was once considered one of the biggest threats to internal security.In reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha,  Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai said that this has been achieved with resolute implementation of the National Policy and Action Plan to address Left-Wing Extremism 2015 and the coordinated efforts of Centre and State governments. He informed the House that at present, no district is categorized as LWE affected. Mr Rai added that the number of Naxal-affected districts reduced from 126 to 90 in April 2018, 70 in July 2021, 38 in April 2024, 8 in December 2025 and zero in March 2026.The Minister also informed that  at present, 37 districts are categorized as Legacy and Thrust districts, which are no more LWE affected, but continued support regarding security and development measures is required for some more time to consolidate the position. He informed that one district has been kept under the category of District of Concern where LWE violent activities have been totally contained and their organizational structure has been completely dismantled.The Minister said that in the post-LWE scenario, the focus is on saturation of government welfare programmes, strengthening local self-governance, facilitating the rehabilitation of surrendered cadres and expanding the reach of governance and public services in remote areas. Mr Rai said that overall, Centre is committed for ensuring security and accelerated development of erstwhile LWE affected districts of the country.

. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) today claimed that its Aerospace Force targeted a US air base and the US Central Command (CENTCOM) headquarters in Jordan with ballistic missiles.The IRGC said the strikes were carried out in response to US military attacks on Iran and vowed to continue operations until US threats, illegal and hostile moves end, the official Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA) reported. The claim comes amid renewed tensions in West Asia following military exchanges between Iran and the US.Meanwhile, the US military said it intercepted multiple ballistic missiles launched from Iran in what it described as an attempted “surprise attack” on American forces in the region.US Central Command said on X that , Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps launched multiple ballistic missiles at US forces in the Middle East in an attempted surprise attack. It added that all missiles were intercepted and US forces remained on high alert.

. India’s boxing juggernaut rolled on at the Commonwealth Games as reigning world champion Jaismine Lamboria stormed into the women’s 57 kg semifinals with a hard-fought victory over England’s Elise Glynn today, assuring the country of yet another medal. Displaying tactical maturity, composure and sharp counter-punching, Lamboria edged the closely contested quarterfinal to become the 10th Indian boxer to secure at least a bronze medal in Glasgow with the semi finals scheduled for Friday.The victory extends India’s remarkable boxing campaign, with the contingent now guaranteed double-digit medals.Earlier, Preeti Pawar (54kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg), Sakshi Choudhary (51kg), Arundhati Choudhary (70kg), Lovlina Borgohain (75kg), Jadumani Singh Mandengbam (55kg), Sachin Siwach (60kg), Ankush Panghal (80kg) and Narender Berwal (90 kg) had also booked semifinal berths.National record holder Animesh Kujur clocked his season’s best time to qualify for the 200 metre semifinals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow today.The 23-year-old Kujur clocked 20.46 seconds to win Heat 4 of the first round, finishing ahead of Cameroon’s Emmanuel Eseme, who had clinched the 100m gold yesterday with a time of 9.83 seconds.Kujur qualified seventh overall among the 16 semifinalists, while Eseme, who recorded 20.73 seconds in the heats, advanced in 14th place.The 16 fastest from across 10 heats advanced to the semi-finals to be held tomorrow.

. At the ongoing Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow, Gulveer Singh scripted history by becoming the first Indian athlete to win a medal in the men’s 10,000-metre race after claiming a silver medal. The reigning Asian champion clocked 27:49.78 at the Scotstoun Stadium to finish behind Australia’s Ky Robinson.Harjinder Kaur also added a silver to India’s medal tally in the women’s 69-kilogramme weightlifting event. The 29-year-old Indian weightlifter finished with a combined lift of 227 kilograms to secure India’s seventh medal from eight weightlifting events in Glasgow. This was Harjinder Kaur’s second successive Commonwealth Games medal, after she won bronze at Birmingham in 2022. With this, India’s total medal count at the Glasgow Games rose to 12, including two gold, seven silver and three bronze medals.President Droupadi Murmu and Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan congratulated Gulveer Singh and Harjinder Kaur on their silver medal wins at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games 2026.Meanwhile, four Indian boxers have secured guaranteed bronze medals and will aim to convert them into silver or gold when they compete in the semifinals.Lovlina Borgohain secured India’s first guaranteed medal in the women’s 75-kilogramme event, while Preeti Pawar progressed to the women’s 54-kilogramme semifinals. Priya Ghanghas assured herself of at least a bronze medal by defeating Scotland’s Niamh Mitchell 4-1 in her women’s 60-kilogramme quarterfinal match. Jadumani Singh Mandengbam also stormed into the men’s 55-kilogramme semifinals, extending India’s guaranteed boxing medal tally.

. India has strongly condemned recent attacks on several maritime vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, saying that targeting commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure in the region must end.Permanent Representative of India to the United Nations, Parvathaneni Harish, said that after a brief pause in the ongoing conflict in the region, there has been a worrying resumption of attacks and escalation of hostilities. Mr Harish voiced India’s strong condemnation of attacks on several vessels, including GFS Galaxy, MT Al Bahiyah and MT Mombasa, during their transit through the Strait of Hormuz this month. He said that free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways must be restored.

. The Lok Sabha today passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. The Bill seeks to amend the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024. The legislation incorporates several significant provisions, including stringent penalties such as imprisonment for up to ten years, fines of up to ten crore rupees, and the seizure of the properties of convicted offenders. To ensure the expeditious disposal of cases, the legislation mandates that every State Government and Union Territory Administration establish Special Fast Track Courts for the day-to-day trial. It further provides that investigations into offences must be completed within two months from the date the information is recorded at the police station. The trials must be concluded within three months from the filing of the chargesheet.Replying to the discussion on the bill, Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Dr Jitendra Singh said, the amendment in the bill has been brought to make the law more stringent and ensure speedy justice. He said, the new Bill is a reaffirmation of the government’s commitment to safeguard the welfare of students and youth. Dr Singh said, the incidents of paper leaks have taken place in various states ruled by different parties.Hitting out at the Opposition for their conduct, Dr Singh said that when an important bill is being discussed, the Opposition is playing politics, instead of offering suggestions. He also criticised Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi for using unparliamentary language, saying it is inappropriate and unfortunate. Replying to Mr Gandhi’s accusation against Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Dr Singh said that the government repeatedly clarified that no shots were fired and only tear gas was used. He said, since no shots were fired, the question of issuing an order does not arise as the authority to issue such an order rests with the magistrate, not the Minister.Earlier, participating in the discussion, JDU MP Dileshwar Kamait expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for bringing the Bill in Parliament, stating that it will ensure a brighter future for students while enhancing transparency in the education system. He said that the bill has been brought in the interest of students. Mr Kamait added that the new legislation provides for time-bound investigations and stringent punishment to ensure accountability and curb malpractices.Opposing the bill, N K Premachandran of RSP said that the bill is inadequate to achieve the purpose stated in the bill. He alleged that the changes brought in the proposed bill are merely cosmetic.Participating in the discussion, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said that the education system in the country has now become very expensive. He alleged that the money spent on conducting NEET-UG examination is more than the education budget of the country. Mr Gandhi said that the Students’ protest on the NEET issue was not violence or hatred but a deep expression of the youth, and all political parties must respect this expression.Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju strongly objected to the remarks of Rahul Gandhi against Union Home Minister Amit Shah. Mr Rijiju demanded that Mr Gandhi should apologise in the House for his remarks.  Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also requested Mr Gandhi to speak only on the bill and do not level allegations without any facts. The House also witnessed two brief adjournments during the discussion. After passing the bill, Mr Birla adjourned the House till 11:00 AM tomorrow.

. At the ongoing Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, nine Indian boxers have assured medals for the country after sealing semifinal berths. Five pugilists including Arundhati Choudhary in women’s 70 kg, Sakshi Chaudhary in women’s 51kg, Sachin in Men’s 60kg, Ankush Panghal in men’s 80kg semifinals and Narender Berwal in men’s 90 Plus kg categoreis registered victories today.Earlier, Lovlina Borgohain in 75 kg, Preeti Pawar in 54 kg, Priya Ghanghas in 60 kg and Jadumani Singh in Men’s 55kg had already reached semifinals confirming medals for India.India’s overall medal tally currently stands at 12 comprising two Gold, seven Silver and three Bronze.

. The Supreme Court today agreed to hear a batch of pleas alleging excessive use of police force against students protesting over the issue of examination paper leaks tomorrow. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also agreed to take up a separate plea, filed by a few family members of those police personnel who were attacked during the protest, along with other listed petitions. Chief Justice Surya Kant today observed that the right to peaceful and lawful protest is constitutionally protected. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, said he will assist the court.Meanwhile, hearing another plea filed by RJD MP Sudhakar Singh following the cancellation of the NEET-UG held on May 3 over alleged paper leak and the announcement of re-NEET, the Court said it will see what the Nandan Nilekani-led high-powered task force formed by the government suggests on the online conduct of the NEET examination. A bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said some out-of-the-box suggestions are needed especially when transition is made from the physical mode to the online conduct of the NEET examination.

. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju criticised Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi claiming that he used unparliamentary words in Lok Sabha today and wrongly accused Home Minister Amit Shah. Talking to media outside Parliament, Mr Rijiju stressed that the Home Minister or any other minister do not give order for firing. He said these are the orders to be passed by the magistrate or the SDM who are present at that particular place. He added that as a Parliamentary Affairs Minister, he looks forward to the Leader of the Opposition making some substantive intervention.

. Polling has begun for by-elections to three Assembly constituencies in Bihar, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh. Voting is taking place for the Bankipur constituency in Bihar, Manjalpur in Gujarat and Datia in Madhya Pradesh. Polling, which began at 7 AM, will continue till 6 PM.In Bihar, the bye-election for the Bankipur seat was necessitated after BJP President Nitin Nabin vacated the Assembly seat following his election to the Rajya Sabha.In Gujarat’s Manjalpur Assembly seat, the BJP has fielded Satish Patel, while the Congress has pitted Bhikhabhai Rabari against him. The Election Commission has introduced 100 per cent webcasting, mobile deposit counters outside polling stations and cVIGIL facilities for online complaints related to the Model Code of Conduct. The by-election was necessitated due to the death of BJP MLA Yogesh Patel, who had represented the Manjalpur Assembly constituency multiple times.In Madhya Pradesh, the Datia seat became vacant due to the disqualification of Rajendra Bharti.
. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 21 paise to end at 95 rupees and 64 paise against the US dollar.

. In Japan, a powerful 7.1 magnitude earthquake struck southern Kumamoto Prefecture, knocking out power to thousands of homes, rupturing roads, and injuring at least 50 people. Several people were reportedly trapped inside a partially collapsed shopping mall. Japan’s disaster management agency said around 3 lakh residents have been advised to evacuate to designated shelters. Several buildings caught fire or partially collapsed, while large cracks appeared on roads, including an elevated highway.Transport services were severely disrupted, with flights grounded. The Kyushu Railway Company said all train services, including the Kyushu Shinkansen, have been halted following the earthquake.Authorities have also issued a tsunami advisory for the coasts of the Ariake Sea and the Yatsushiro Sea but was lifted within two hours. Meanwhile, the operators of the Genkai Nuclear Power Station in Saga Prefecture and the Sendai Nuclear Power Station in Kagoshima Prefecture said they are conducting inspections to determine whether either facility has sustained any abnormalities.Meanwhile, Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the government has set up a task force to gather information, assess possible damage and prepare for rescue operations if needed.

. The UN Human Rights Office has voiced concern over Islamabad’s crackdown on peaceful protesters in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. Over 40 civilians were killed and several others injured in the firing by Pakistani forces on protesters during a march organised by the Joint Awami Action Committee from Rawalakot to Muzaffarabad on Monday.UN Human Rights Office spokesperson Jeremy Laurence said the criminalisation of a civil society organisation and restrictions on public gatherings raise serious concerns about violations of the rights to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and association.Amid escalating unrest in the occupied territory, a human rights body Jammu Kashmir Human Rights Observatory has urged the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights to intervene over reports of lethal force being used against peaceful protesters.Meanwhile, Pakistani authorities have revoked the registrations of 13 private schools in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, alleging the involvement of their management, staff and students in the ongoing protests.On the other hand, British Kashmiris staged a protest outside the Pakistani Consulate in Birmingham today over reports of civilian deaths in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir.

. India’s first-ever direct commercial container freight train has reached Nepal, marking a new chapter in rail-based cross-border freight movement. The Railway Ministry said that the train, comprising 40 wagons carrying a consignment of canola, completed its journey under the revised India-Nepal Rail Transit Protocol.  The successful operation enables direct rail movement of containerised cargo from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar without transshipment at the border. The new arrangement is expected to reduce transit time, logistics costs and cargo handling while improving the efficiency, reliability and competitiveness of cross-border trade between the two neighbouring countries.The Ministry said that the direct freight service is also expected to provide a significant boost to the movement of import and export cargo by offering a faster, more economical and environmentally sustainable mode of transportation. It added that by reducing multiple handling points and improving supply chain efficiency, the initiative will benefit exporters, importers, logistics operators and industries engaged in cross-border trade.

. In squash, India’s men and women teams advanced to the quarterfinals of the World Junior Squash Team Championships in Ontario, Canada. The fifth-seeded Indian men defeated 11th-seeded Kuwait 2-1 in the pre-quarterfinals .Yusha Nafees lost the opening match in straight games to Abdullah Ali, but Aryaveer Dewan leveled the tie with an 11-5, 11-6, 11-5 victory over Khaled Walead Al Fouzain. Gurveer Singh then sealed the win with an 11-3, 11-3, 11-4 triumph against Abdul Rahman Al Sanea. India will face England in the quarterfinals.The Indian women completed the group stage with a dominant 3-nil win over South Africa. Rudra Singh defeated Makayla Naidoo 11-4, 11-5, 11-3 before Anahat Singh cruised past Brianna Robinson 11-1, 11-1, 11-3. Saanvi Kalanki completed the sweep with an 11-4, 11-3, 11-3 victory over Vivienne Van Der Schyff. India’s women will take on the United States in the quarterfinals.
